headline: Nvidia earnings after the close; the AI selloff hit a 2.67% Nasdaq-100 drop on 16 Nov

what_happened.summary: Per the Cboe Daily Take 'Nvidia Tugs Market Lower Again' (16 Nov), Nvidia fell about another 4% and the AI and semiconductor complex led the market lower, with selling spreading beyond tech. FRED shows the Nasdaq-100 closed at 27197.15 (-2.67%) and the S&P 500 at 7416.59 (-1.92%). Volatility jumped: VIX 22.91, VXN 32.9, VVIX 114.23 and COR1M 16.42 (+39.15%). Yields eased (10-year 5.12%, -3.0 bp), so this was an AI and equity move rather than a rates shock. Nvidia reports after the US close today, its first call since the CEO resignation, and the Cboe Macro Volatility Digest (week of 16 Nov) says options imply an 8% one-day move.
what_happened.market_action: Nasdaq-100 -2.67% vs S&P 500 -1.92% (FRED). The Cboe Daily Take says the Nasdaq Composite and S&P fell for a third straight session and that investors moved into consumer staples. VIX9D rose 29.91% to 23.15, so near-dated hedging jumped. The Daily Take quotes VIX at 23.56 (+22%), while the Cboe index series in the data block shows 22.91 (+18.70%); this brief uses the data-block figure. Morning headlines (unverified) conflict on whether Nasdaq futures are up or down, and no live price is in the inputs.
what_happened.macro: Treasury (official): 2-year 4.83% (-5.0 bp), 10-year 5.12% (-3.0 bp), 30-year 5.46% (-1.0 bp). Polymarket (prediction-market prices, not CME FedWatch) has a 25 bps December hike at 92.5% and 50+ bps at 4.7%. The Cboe Digest says ~7% of a 50 bps hike is priced in the OIS market. BLS: October CPI +0.35% m/m (prior +0.65%), core CPI +0.3%, PPI final demand 6.52% y/y. Retail sales and import/export prices were due at 14:30 CET, and no print is in the inputs yet.
what_happened.geopolitics: The Cboe Daily Take says WTI fell 3.4% to $85.57 on signs of recovering Strait of Hormuz flows and a forecast fourth-quarter supply surplus. Official FRED oil data are stale to 11 Nov (WTI 89.62). One headline (unverified) says oil rebounded on Trump questioning the need for an Iran deal.
what_happened.company_news: Cboe says Nvidia is being hit by the leadership transition and by doubts over the sustainability of AI spending. Options imply an 8.5% move (Daily Take) or 8% (Digest), against an average realized move of 4.8% over the past four quarters. The Digest says put buying was 32% of Nvidia retail opening trades on Cboe on Thursday, vs a 21% year-to-date average. Disney (9% implied move) and Home Depot (just under 5%) also report, per the Daily Take.

driver_reason: The Cboe Daily Take attributes the 16 Nov selloff mainly to Nvidia and the AI trade, while yields fell and so did not drive the move. Nvidia's results and guidance after the close are the next large catalyst.
leader_reason: The Nasdaq-100 underperformed the S&P 500 by 0.75 pct pts on the last session and by 0.78 pct pts over five sessions. VXN is 9.99 pts above VIX, so tech carries the stress. Engine read: QQQ leads in the sense that Nasdaq-100 weakness is setting the market's direction; COR1M rising to 16.42 hints at some spread beyond tech.

overlap_with_previous.echo_check: The morning headlines repeat the 'ahead of Nvidia earnings' theme without new facts, and they disagree on futures direction, so they are treated as an echo. The Nvidia theme itself has new evidence (price move, options pricing, retail positioning), so it is not an echo. The Fed-hike theme adds little new evidence beyond small odds changes.

scheduled_events.why_it_matters: This is the key test of the AI trade and the first Nvidia call since the CEO left. Options imply an 8% to 8.5% move. It falls after the regular session, so it affects the next session's open more than today's close.
Housing data, which the Cboe post describes as soft for October. Lower importance than the Fed and Nvidia.
Could show how divided the committee is on the December hike. Polymarket gives 73.0% for zero dissents in December.

next_day.confidence_reason: This horizon is today's session, which closes before Nvidia reports. Pre-earnings positioning, the retail sales print and headlines that disagree on futures direction all weigh on it, and my last next_day forecast missed by a wide margin.

record_comment: Only one forecast is graded: the 13 Nov next_day forecast (Brier 0.697 vs 0.667 for equal odds). My top pick (base) was wrong because the -2.67% move breached the -1.0 cut. Cuts of ±1.0 were too tight for this volatility, so I have widened them.

Polymarket has a 25 bps December hike at 92.5% and 50+ bps at 4.7%. Nvidia reports after the close Tue 17 Nov with an implied move of 8% to 8.5%, its first call since the CEO resigned. Retail sales (14:30 CET) and FOMC minutes (Wed 20:00 CET) are the other catalysts. Credit showed no stress as of 13 Nov (HY OAS 3.23). Oil data are stale.
